# Independent audit: active contact area and centroid erosion cost

Audited the complete source
`candidate 0c3c4405d9ae2dd3`,
including its use of Section 5 of
`candidate 72bbac9873894c0b`
and the common-area theorem proved in
`candidate d332d092619053f4`.


one-witness compatible-descent criterion, not an arbitrary-body depth
theorem.

1. If L subset K and their support values agree at n, every point of
   L(n) lies on K(n). The exceptional nonregular K boundary is null for
   the SAME ambient H_(d-1) measure, so intersecting it with boundary L
   does not create a positive exceptional mass. At the other points the
   unique K normal equals n. This proves domination after restricting
   BOTH area measures to the Borel contact set Z, including singular
   area measures. No false monotonicity of area measures under unrestricted
   body inclusion is used.

2. Restricting S_A wedge S_B<=S_M to Z and then applying the preceding
   inclusion statement to M subset K gives exactly (2). In d=1 it is
   the direct common-endpoint statement for H_0 atoms.

3. At the actual centroid source the projective minimizer is a=0 by
   the proved uniqueness and centroid stationarity. Hence f(1)=1 and
   the source boundary speed is H(n)=h_(K-y)(n)>0. Its total loss is
   D=integral H dS_K=d|K|, and each source-containing cap loses at least
   Gamma_d D. This keeps original unweighted volume throughout.

4. Both one-input speeds are 2H, with no physical-point dependence.
   Multiplication by one positive Borel function commutes with the
   measure wedge, so their overlap cost is exactly
   2 integral_Z H d(S_A wedge S_B). Contact-area domination bounds it
   by 2R. The cutoff/allocation/shape limits are taken in the proper
   order; neither exact continuous attainment nor a derivative through
   a shrinking contact band is assumed.

5. Nested endpoint erosions have nonnegative cap losses even for
   supporting full/empty traces. A finite fixed cap cover whose rows all
   contain the assigned interior source therefore has loss at least
   Gamma_d D per row. Total loss is D+C, so the strict surplus is
   Gamma_d D-beta(D+C). The original fixed covers and the assumed
   persistent slack, not new centers inferred from first moments,
   turn this into a global normalized-depth descent. Under these premises
   beta>0 automatically: a cap containing an interior point of a
   positive-volume source captures positive source volume. Thus the
   displayed choice of C using division by beta has no zero case.

6. If R<=D/2 and beta<Gamma_d/2, then
   (Gamma_d-beta)D-beta(2R)>=(Gamma_d-2beta)D>0.
   If only R<=D is known, the corresponding sufficient bound is
   beta<Gamma_d/3. Both strict constants and the direction of the
   resulting necessary contact-area condition are correct.

The stated hypothesis that one assigned source cover controls every
deepest base is essential. This audit does not replace it by independent
circuits at several sources, nor assert simultaneous freedom of those
sources at their active contacts.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
